title: hysteresis-backpressure-controller-and-client-window-adaptive-prefetch
author: Marina Lopez
description:
Motivation: streaming tails and emission oscillation under mixed workloads still cause visible TTFB spikes for latency-sensitive tenants. Timers-only flush cadence (fixed tick sizes) leads to under/over-emission when client request patterns change quickly, and aggressive prefetching causes unnecessary KV churn on multi-tenant hosts. This PR introduces a hysteresis-driven backpressure controller plus a per-client adaptive emission window and lightweight KV prefetch hints to reduce oscillation and lower first-byte latency across the board.

What changed (summary): 1) Emission controller: replace simple token-tick flusher with an event-driven controller that maintains a soft credit per stream and applies hysteresis thresholds to avoid flip-flopping between emit/no-emit states. Credits decay slowly and are replenished based on successful kernel pulls and observed downstream ACKs. 2) Client window adaptivity: per-client EMA of inter-request inter-arrival is used to size a short emission window (micro-window) so we coalesce only when beneficial for latency and throughput. 3) KV prefetch hints: when a micro-window is extended we emit a non-blocking KV prefetch hint that primes the cache for the expected key range; hints are lightweight and do not allocate KV reservations. 4) Kernel alignment: emission windows are aligned to kernel batch boundaries using a small jitter buffer to improve kernel coalescing without raising worst-case latency. 5) Telemetry and rollout: new metrics (emit_state_transitions, hysteresis_skips, kv_prefetch_hints) and a feature flag (runtime.hysteresis_backpressure) with gradual rollout.

Benchmarks: internal canary on Dedicated pools (A100) using mixed short/long prompt workload: median TTFB -12%, p95 -32% when feature enabled and conservative hysteresis settings used. CPU/GPU utilization stable; KV cache hit rate improved ~6% for the tested multi-tenant profile.

Related: complements prior microbatch/pacing work (ENG-??) but targets oscillation and prefetch cost; aligns with the Optimize team's request to reduce cross-tenant KV churn (ENG-4899).

Testing and safety: unit tests for controller state machine, integration test simulating bursty clients, and a stress job that validates no regressions in throughput. Feature gated and default-off for some internal clouds until rollout completes.

Merge notes: squash-merge after CI green. See release notes for feature flag usage and suggested knob defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted.
